anqr.title: Appraisal Suite: Annual Network Quality Report Framework 26-27

egw.title: EASE Growth: Workflow, Roles & Stage Gates 26-27

essentials.title: Read the Subject Specialists' visit reports as they come in
essentials.description: As Academic Director you receive each report within 5 working days of the visit. Check the findings are specific and the agreed next steps have an owner and a date, and ask for revisions where they do not.

source.quote: The visit report is read by the Eduversal Academic Director (who needs strategic intelligence about the school)

essentials.title: Act on academic concerns escalated through the Academic Board
essentials.description: The CAO receives the academic-quality picture and the concerns raised by Subject Specialists and the Academic Board. Support follows evidence: diagnosis, a clear development action and a defined review point.
essentials.timing_text: Every week, and whenever a concern is escalated

source.quote: Receives the academic-quality picture, Academic Board reporting, School Appraisal outcomes, academic trends, and escalated academic concerns.

essentials.title: Give final sign-off before any Common Assessment is published
essentials.description: Sign off only after the question set has been peer-reviewed by a second Subject Specialist and confirmed by the Academic Board. No test goes live without this sign-off (CAO).
essentials.timing_text: Whenever a Teacher-Paced or Synchronized Test is ready for release

source.quote: Final sign-off is given by the CAO before any Common Assessment is published on Latihan.id or sent to schools for paper-based use.

essentials.title: Act at once on any Critical Attention case
essentials.description: Join the Visit I Supervisor's follow-up for a school in Critical Attention; its action plan is due within 2 weeks of the visit report. Keep school-specific risk information in a separate confidential record.
essentials.timing_text: As soon as a school's outcome is Critical Attention

source.quote: A Critical Attention case must never be delayed while waiting for annual reporting.

essentials.title: Keep coaching and journal content out of Principal Appraisal
essentials.description: Coaching is a private growth space: neither its content nor its participation data enters F5 or any other score. The Foundation Representative has no access to coaching records either.

source.quote: As the appraiser, you will not see coaching records, and you must not ask for them.

tasks.title: Confirm Visit Supervisor assignments and the Phase 1 schedule
tasks.description: The CAO confirms each school's Visit I and Visit II Supervisors with the experts (1 July), tells the schools (8 July) and confirms the Phase 1 visit dates (10 July). The CAO then leads the online Phase 0 Kickoffs with the Supervisors.
tasks.timing_text: 1–10 July 2026, before teaching starts (shown in the first teaching week); Kickoffs 15 July – 27 August

source.quote: Confirm School Supervisor assignments with all experts

tasks.title: Run the start-of-year gate with the Academic Board
tasks.description: Confirm Subject Specialist portfolios, subject responsibilities, the school network list, the authoritative documents and who writes which assessments. Agree the year's priorities.

source.quote: Roles, school portfolios, authoritative documents, assessment responsibilities, and annual priorities are confirmed.

tasks.title: Follow up Academic Board decisions and network priorities
tasks.description: Check that agreed decisions have an owner, a deadline and real follow-up, and look at network trends and cross-school support actions against the agreed priorities.

source.quote: Strategic academic priorities with review points, system-quality monitoring, Academic Board decision follow-up, network trend analysis, cross-school support actions

tasks.title: Confirm each principal's appraisal set-up in writing
tasks.description: Send each principal their level, primary appraiser, F2 windows, 360 windows, F5 points and evidence channels before any scored evidence. Year 1 principals are in protected induction and are not appraised.
tasks.timing_text: Before each principal's scored cycle begins, and before the September–October observation window

source.quote: Eduversal confirms their appraisal level, primary appraiser, two F2 visit windows, 360 windows, and the evidence channels that will be used.

tasks.title: Carry out or assign the first leadership observation visits
tasks.description: Use the eight foci P1–P8 and record honest, evidence-based notes. Where practical the visit can share travel with a School Appraisal visit, but the two keep separate evidence and records.

source.quote: F2 (Observation) — collected during at least two scheduled visits, in the Sept–Oct and Feb–Apr windows.

tasks.title: Carry out or assign the second leadership observation visits
tasks.description: Schedule this visit separately: both on-site School Appraisal visits are in Semester I. Each principal needs two valid F2 records before the year-end appraisal.

source.quote: is the primary appraiser, owns the full record, and conducts or assigns at least two leadership observation visits.

tasks.title: Run the Semester I gate with the Academic Board
tasks.description: Review completed deliverables, overdue actions and unresolved risks, then reset priorities for Semester II from the evidence.

source.quote: The Board reviews progress against actions and resets priorities from evidence.

tasks.title: Read each Annual School Quality Report as it arrives
tasks.description: Each domain keeps its own Development Rating: read them side by side and never average them into one school score. Note where the two School Development Priorities need Eduversal support.
tasks.timing_text: Within 3 weeks of each Phase 3 visit; every report is due by 11 December 2026

source.quote: Distribution: Eduversal CAO, School Principal, and Academic Coordinator.

tasks.title: Decide any School Appraisal appeals
tasks.description: A school may appeal a domain rating within 10 working days of receiving its report. Review it with the relevant Domain Lead and reply within 15 working days; the CAO's decision is final.
tasks.timing_text: Within 15 working days of each appeal (most arrive after the December reports)

source.quote: The CAO reviews the appeal with the relevant Domain Lead and responds within 15 working days.

tasks.title: Update the network academic-quality picture after Phase 3
tasks.description: Read the five domain ratings next to academic results, EASE school-level summaries and Academic Board reporting in the Academic Quality Overview. It keeps D1–D5 separate and creates no new rating.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: early Semester II, once all Annual School Quality Reports are in

source.quote: The role is to identify academic strengths, risks, and network priorities, and to ensure that agreed School Development Priorities lead to measurable improvement over time.

tasks.title: Hold the termly IPDL review with each Subject Specialist
tasks.description: Treat it as a development conversation: their goals, evidence and impact statements, and specific outputs they want feedback on. For a new Specialist still in induction, you also sign off phase transitions.
tasks.timing_text: Once a term (shown near the end of each semester)

source.quote: Every Subject Specialist at Eduversal maintains an IPDL from the first day of employment. It is reviewed termly with the Academic Director.

tasks.title: Confirm the EASE Academic blueprint and sign off the paper
tasks.description: With the Academic Board, check the blueprint, syllabus references and preparation resources are current, then give the CAO sign-off on the questions. Individual results stay confidential and never enter appraisal.
tasks.timing_text: Before each EASE Academic sitting (5 December 2026 and 15 May 2027)

source.quote: Before each assessment window, the Academic Board should confirm that the blueprint, syllabus references, and examinable resources are current.

tasks.title: Sign off the EASE Growth package after full-package review
tasks.description: Sign off only when peer review, the full-package checks and the Academic Board review are complete. Version 1 is a baseline: never describe it as growth or use it to rank schools.
tasks.timing_text: Before each EASE Growth sitting: Growth I (28 Sep 2026), Primary (January 2027), Growth II (29 Mar 2027)

source.quote: CAO gives final sign-off only after full-package review is complete.

tasks.title: Check every principal's evidence set is complete
tasks.description: Confirm level and weights, two valid F2 records, the 360 threshold and the late-year summative 360 cycle, the F4 sources and F5. Without F5 the appraisal stays incomplete.

source.quote: confirm F5 is complete — if it is not, the appraisal remains incomplete and no final composite, band or recommendation is issued;

tasks.title: Finalise and sign off each Principal Appraisal
tasks.description: Hold the growth conversation, record the principal's reflection, agree 2–3 next-year goals and sign off the record. Give the Foundation Representative only the summary triplet and goals for co-signature.
tasks.timing_text: Year end (shown in the last teaching week)

source.quote: The appraiser reviews it all, writes the narrative reflections, sets the recommendation, and finalizes.

tasks.title: Prepare the Annual Network Quality Report
tasks.description: Report D1–D5 as five separate network profiles, add Phase 4 impact and the common priority themes, and anonymise schools. No ranking, no league table and no single network score.
tasks.timing_text: After the Phase 4 Impact Reviews (May–June 2027; shown in the last teaching week)

source.quote: to identify anonymized strengths, common development needs, and future support priorities without ranking schools or creating a composite network quality score.

tasks.title: Run the year-end gate with the Academic Board
tasks.description: Record what changed, what shows impact and what remains unresolved, update the Source-of-Truth Register and make sure no high-risk issue is lost in the handover to next year.
tasks.timing_text: June (shown in the last teaching week)

source.quote: The Board records what changed, what evidence shows impact, what remains unresolved, and what must change next year.

tasks.title: Decide whether the Scorecard Layer should carry weight next year
tasks.description: This year it carries 0% weight. Use feedback from Domain Leads and school leaders after the first full cycle before deciding on any blend.
tasks.timing_text: After the first full cycle (end of AY 2026-2027)

source.quote: Review whether to introduce a qualitative/quantitative blend after cycle 1 (weight is 0% this year)

notes_for_reviewer: What was wrong in v1 (director.json): (1) a 40-week year with fixed week numbers; the real year has 36 teaching weeks. (2) The annual Principal Appraisal sat in late June as a one-off; live: two F2 observation windows (Sept–Oct 2026, Feb–Apr 2027), F3 from the late-year 360 cycle, then year-end finalisation and sign-off by the CAO / designated Academic Director. (3) It talked about 'partner-school relationships at the principal/yayasan level' and signing off yayasan RKT/RKAS; the live documents give the Director no such duty, and the Foundation Representative / yayasan receives only the summary triplet and goals. (4) Invented routines with no live basis: weekly Specialist huddle, weekly touch-base with 3 principals, monthly report to the CEO/Board, termly Cambridge International liaison, 'QAR aggregation', 'EPDP' labels, 'NN3 cert holder' as principal observer (NN codes belong to the Induction Charter). (5) 'Approve the Sem-1 Common Assessment paper in November'; live: the CAO signs off every Common Assessment before it is published, all year. (6) 'Oversee Sem-2 Specialist visit cycle Feb–Apr'; both on-site School Appraisal visits are in Semester I. Also 'HQ' throughout and a 'compliance' priority level.

Who is 'the Director'? The live documents give these duties to three labels: 'CAO' (Common Assessment, EASE Academic and EASE Growth sign-off; Phase 0 with the Supervisors; Supervisor assignments; appeals; Academic Quality Overview), 'Chief Academic Officer / designated HQ Academic Director' (Principal Appraisal primary appraiser) and 'Academic Director' (Subject Specialists' supervisor: visit reports, termly IPDL review, Specialist induction sign-offs). Each description says which. If the CH 'director' sub-role covers Directors who are not the CAO, please decide which of DR2-003, DR2-006, DR2-013–DR2-015, DR2-017, DR2-018 and DR2-023 they should see.

Sign-off conflict: Specialist Guide §5 says 'Final papers are signed off by the Academic Director before distribution to schools' and its production table gives 'Academic Director sign-off' for EASE papers, while EASE Assessment: Standards, EASE Academic and the EASE Growth workflow all give final sign-off to the CAO. DR2-003, DR2-017 and DR2-018 follow the EASE documents.

DR2-004 description uses the School Development Plan rule that a Critical Attention action plan is due within 2 weeks of the visit report (Appraisal Suite: School Development Plan 26-27); the quote comes from the Annual Network Quality Report Framework.

The Annual Network Quality Report Framework does not name its author; Quality Oversight §2.2 says the CAO's evidence 'is synthesized through' it, so DR2-021 is given to the Director and quoted from Quality Oversight. It falls after Phase 4 (May–June), so it shows in the last teaching week.

Dates the live documents do not give: the two Principal Appraisal 360 cycles ('mid-year' formative, 'late-year / year-end' summative) and the F5 termly self-assessment points — folded into DR2-009 and DR2-019 descriptions instead of separate tasks. The written set-up confirmation (DR2-009) is placed on 17 Aug as a suggestion before the first F2 window.

Principal Coordination Meetings / 3-day Workshop (5–7 Oct 2026, 5–7 Apr 2027) appear only in the Academic Board Master Timeline (a Sheet, owner 'Academic Services / Academic Board'); no Doc describes the Director's part, so they are not tasks. Same for the weekly Academic Board meeting (the Meeting Minutes show it, but no document sets the cadence).

Certification Programme: the Governance Decision records Academic Board confirmation and CAO / Academic Director sign-off as 'Approved', live status PRE-RELEASE; later major changes need both approvals. Event-driven, so not a weekly task.

Specialist professional review: Induction Module: Overview 26-27 says the Academic Director 'later conducts the professional review' of a new Specialist, but no document gives an annual review date or form for established Specialists. Not added; see ideas.

DR2-018 includes the 28 Sep 2026 Growth I sitting (already past) so the file covers the whole year; the Primary Growth date differs between the brief (18–22 Jan 2027) and the calendar (17–21 Jan 2027) — either way the reminder shows on 11 Jan.

Load (my simulation of the `when` rules over 36 teaching weeks): heaviest week is 3–7 May 2027 with 5 dated tasks (monthly follow-up, Principal Appraisal finalisation, Annual Network Quality Report, year-end gate, Scorecard decision); 13 Jul 2026 and 19 Apr 2027 have 3; most weeks have 0–2. The two F2 windows add one task to every week of Sep–Oct and Feb–Apr. Essentials: 5. Please re-run with the real seeder.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A fixed weekly Academic Board / Specialist team meeting with a standard agenda (visit schedule, escalations, assessment production).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Meeting Minutes show the Board meeting weekly, and the Annual Operating Calendar's weekly rhythm depends on an action tracker, but no document sets the meeting cadence or who chairs it.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Annual Operating Calendar 26-27 (standing weekly rhythm)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: An annual professional review for each established Subject Specialist, with a set date and a short record.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Specialist Guide has termly IPDL reviews and the Induction Module mentions a 'professional review', but there is no year-end review step, form or timing for Specialists after their first year.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Specialist Guide 26-27 §8 (Your Own Professional Growth)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A short termly network report from the CAO to the Executive Director / leadership, drawn from the Academic Quality Overview.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: Quality Oversight describes what the CAO receives but not a regular upward report between the Annual School Quality Reports (December) and the Annual Network Quality Report (June).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Quality Oversight 26-27 §11 (Reporting, Support & Escalation)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: State the Director's / CAO's role in the two Principal Coordination Meetings (October and April) and what each must produce.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The meetings are in the Master Timeline as 'Critical' but no Doc says who leads them or what network priorities they should confirm.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Academic Board: Annual Operating Calendar 26-27 (October and April sections)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A regular, light contact routine between the CAO / Academic Director and each principal outside appraisal visits.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: Principals meet the appraiser mainly in the F2 windows; a non-evaluative contact rhythm would surface problems early. It must stay separate from Principal Appraisal evidence and from coaching.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A scheduled contact with Cambridge International (regional team) each semester for centre-level news and network issues.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: No live document names an Eduversal owner for the network's relationship with Cambridge International, although several documents depend on current Cambridge rules and dates.
